speaker: control
text: Welcome to Hadley–Apennine. That rover has been parked here since 1971. On its very first drive, its front steering stopped answering. Walk over and take a look.

speaker: control
text: Taurus–Littrow, the last place humans drove on the Moon. See the patched fender on the right rear wheel? That home-made fix is why we are here. Go and inspect it.

speaker: control
text: Gusev Crater. Spirit has been stuck here at Troy since 2009, and its right-front wheel died in 2006. Walk over and find out what went wrong.

speaker: control
text: Perseverance Valley. Opportunity fell silent here in June 2018, when a dust storm covered the whole planet. Let’s find out how it lost its power.

speaker: control
text: Steering checks out. Now a science drive: Hadley Rille, St. George crater and Spur crater, in any order. Stop inside each ring and collect a sample.

speaker: control
text: Fender’s on. And just in time: we have an emergency call.

speaker: control
text: All units: geologist Ana Ruiz is stranded near the South Massif with a dead rover battery. Take her the spare battery before her reserve runs low.

speaker: control
text: We can’t fix that wheel from here, and sunlight won’t fix it either. But winter is coming. We need Spirit on a north-facing slope, so its panels tilt toward the low Sun and make enough power to keep its heaters running.

speaker: control
text: Your power pack has given Spirit just enough charge for a short drive. Spinning wheels in sand burn energy for nothing, so go slow.

speaker: control
text: Opportunity’s panels are clean and its battery is charged, but only just. Drive it up to the ridge with a clear view of Earth and send its science report.

speaker: narrator
text: Hadley Rille is a winding channel more than a kilometre wide, probably carved by flowing lava. Scott and Irwin sampled its rim on their first drive.

speaker: narrator
text: At St. George crater the crew collected breccias: rocks shattered by impacts and welded back together. They record the Moon’s violent early history.

speaker: narrator
text: At Spur crater Scott and Irwin found the Genesis Rock: a pale piece of the Moon’s ancient crust, about four billion years old.

speaker: control
text: Not quite. Look closely at the texture and colour, and try again.

speaker: control
text: All three samples are aboard. Bring the crew back to the rocket.

speaker: narrator
text: Without its fender, the rover threw a rooster tail of dust over the crew. Dark dust soaks up sunlight, so dusty suits and equipment can overheat.

speaker: narrator
text: Cernan and Schmitt drove about thirty-six kilometres in this valley, the farthest of any Apollo crew.

speaker: ana
text: You made it! My rover’s battery is completely flat. Grab the spare from your rover and bring it to me.

speaker: ana
text: Line the connector up with the socket, then push it home.

speaker: ana
text: Power’s back! Thank you. I can drive myself home now.

speaker: narrator
text: The map fender was worked out overnight on Earth by astronaut John Young and engineers, then read up to the crew by radio.

speaker: narrator
text: Look at the trail behind the dead wheel. In 2007 Spirit’s dragging wheel uncovered soil like this: about ninety percent silica. On Earth, deposits like this form around hot springs.

speaker: narrator
text: Nearby Home Plate is a layered plateau made by an explosive volcanic eruption, possibly involving water.

speaker: narrator
text: Spirit is in the southern hemisphere, so in winter the Sun stays low in the northern sky. A north-facing slope tilts the panels toward it.

speaker: control
text: You’re on the slope. The panels are tilted toward the Sun, and power is climbing. Spirit can survive the winter here.

speaker: narrator
text: Opportunity found small round blueberries of the mineral hematite, which on Earth usually forms in water.

speaker: narrator
text: Endeavour Crater is about twenty-two kilometres wide. Opportunity spent its last seven years exploring its rim.

speaker: narrator
text: Opportunity drove about forty-five kilometres in total, a record for driving on another world at the time.

speaker: narrator
text: In reality this rover has not moved since 1971. Over three moonwalks it carried Scott and Irwin about twenty-eight kilometres.

speaker: narrator
text: In reality the map fender lasted for the rest of Apollo 17. The rover is still parked near the landing site.

speaker: narrator
text: In reality Spirit never escaped Troy. It last spoke to Earth on the twenty-second of March, 2010.

speaker: narrator
text: In reality Opportunity never answered again after June 2018. NASA declared its mission complete in February 2019.

speaker: control
text: Four machines, four lessons. Curiosity, ingenuity, perseverance, and a legacy that every outpost on the Moon and Mars now stands on. Their journeys ended. Our exploration continues.

speaker: narrator
text: The thirty-first of July, 1971: the first drive. Tilt the T-handle left and right, and watch which wheels turn.

speaker: narrator
text: The front and rear steering had separate circuits. Scott tried switching the forward steering off and on again.

speaker: narrator
text: Test it again. Did cycling the switch help?

speaker: narrator
text: Still nothing, so Scott drove the whole first traverse steering with the rear wheels only. The next morning, they powered up again.

speaker: narrator
text: The front steering worked again on the second moonwalk. Nobody ever found out exactly why.

speaker: narrator
text: The eleventh of December, 1972. The fender extension is gone. Spin the wheel and watch where the dust goes. Anything above the red line lands on the crew.

speaker: capcom
text: Gene, Houston. Let’s try some tape on that extension and see if it holds.

speaker: narrator
text: The tape wouldn’t stick to the dusty fender. In 1972 the piece fell off again during the drive.

speaker: capcom
text: Overnight, John Young and the engineers here worked out a better fix. Take four of your laminated maps and lay them out as one sheet.

speaker: capcom
text: Now tape the maps together along both seams. That gives you a stiff replacement fender.

speaker: capcom
text: Carry the sheet to the back of the right-rear fender, where the extension broke off.

speaker: capcom
text: Hold it on with the two clamps from inside the Lunar Module. Tighten them both, and it won’t depend on tape sticking to dust.

speaker: capcom
text: Nice work. Give the wheel a spin and let’s compare the dust.

speaker: narrator
text: March 2006. Spirit’s right-front wheel has stopped. Send a drive command and watch the motor current and the wheel.

speaker: control
text: The motor gets power, but the wheel won’t turn. Nobody can reach Mars to fix it. So what should the team do?

speaker: narrator
text: Exactly what JPL did. Spirit drove backwards, pulling the dead wheel behind it. Drag the wheel through the soil and see what it uncovers.

speaker: narrator
text: Bright white soil, almost pure silica. A broken wheel led to one of Spirit’s biggest discoveries.

speaker: narrator
text: May 2018. A dust storm is spreading across Mars. Move through the storm and photograph the Sun three times. The dimmer it looks, the thicker the dust.

speaker: control
text: Power is collapsing. Choose which systems stay on, then run the storm. Every combination ends differently, so experiment.

speaker: narrator
text: No combination could save the real Opportunity. Its panels were buried in dust, the cold may have damaged its battery, and more than a thousand wake-up calls went unanswered.
